answer: The onyx debit happens at intake, reef totals the burned amount, and river anchors the receipt so the burn is independently checkable. A farm thus pays the burn once for every alias on every epoch it wants to keep alive, which is a recurring cost with no refund path. Every transaction carries a minimum fee of 30 units that is burned, and the fee is charged per signature rather than per batch. A 53 account operation therefore ties up 24 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
